problem:
Which of the following sets are infinite?

- $A={{f}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $B={{g}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $C={{h}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x)\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following sets are infinite?

- $A={{f}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $B={{g}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(-\operatorname{csc}⁡x)\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $C={{h}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
feedback.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set is the number of elements contained within it. A set is infinite if it has infinitely many elements.

- The set $A$ is finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{(0)}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {f}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {f}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {f}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {f}^{(4)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $A$ contains four elements:

$$
A={-\operatorname{sin}⁡x,-\operatorname{cos}⁡x,\operatorname{sin}⁡x,\operatorname{cos}⁡x}
$$

Consequently, $|A|=4,$ which is finite.

- The set $B$ is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{(0)}(x) & =-\operatorname{csc}⁡x \\ {g}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\operatorname{csc}⁡x)=\operatorname{cot}⁡x\operatorname{csc}⁡x \\ {g}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cot}⁡x\operatorname{csc}⁡x)=\operatorname{csc}⁡x-2{csc}^{3}⁡x \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
B={-\operatorname{csc}⁡x,\operatorname{cot}⁡x\operatorname{csc}⁡x,\operatorname{csc}⁡x-2{csc}^{3}⁡x,…}
$$

Consequently, $B$ is infinite.

- The set $C$ is also infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{(0)}(x) & =\operatorname{cot}⁡x \\ {h}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cot}⁡x)=-{csc}^{2}⁡x \\ {h}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-{csc}^{2}⁡x)=2\operatorname{cot}⁡x{csc}^{2}⁡x \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
C={\operatorname{cot}⁡x,-{csc}^{2}⁡x,2\operatorname{cot}⁡x{csc}^{2}⁡x,…}.
$$

Consequently, $C$ is infinite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ and $C$ only."
